You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The snapshot looks like late 2018. The policy rate is high relative to its own 3-year history (+2.0), and so is the 2-year yield. Unemployment is very low (-2.0) and industrial production is strong. VIX is spiking (+2.5), equities are down about 3% over the month, and credit spreads are widening. Headline CPI has fallen sharply over 3 months, consistent with an oil price drop.

December 2018 fits best on most of these. Equities were down far more than 3% that month, though, and the 12m equity return would not be near -0.5 z. The fit is better for October 2018 (S&P -6.9%) or February 2018.

The 3m headline CPI change of -1.5 points to oil falling, which suggests November or December 2018. In November 2018 the S&P was roughly flat, so 1m equity at -3.0 z does not fit well. The 3m equity change of -1.5 and 12m of -0.5 fit December 2018, when the 12m return was about -4%. A 1m z of -3.0 at -9% is plausible given that the 36-month window had low volatility.

Gold at 0.0 over 1m, 3m at 0.0, and 12m at -1.0 also fits December 2018. The Baa spread 3m change of +1.5 fits as well. The 10y-2y spread is -1.5 z, meaning it was flat relative to a history that included a steeper curve.

I'll go with December 2018.
